posts.name: IrisGo for Solopreneurs
posts.tagline: AI workflow automation: show it once, let it run
posts.description: IrisGo helps solopreneurs automate recurring work. Get daily briefs, triage email, track to-dos, and turn demonstrated tasks into reusable workflows with Watch & Learn. Spend less time on admin and more time building your business. Free during beta.

comments.body:
Hi Product Hunt! 👋 I’m Jeffrey, building IrisGo.

We’re launching an offering for solopreneurs and small business owners who juggle multiple roles, and spend too much time on recurring admin tasks.

https://irisgo.ai/solopreneur

If you’re spending hours each week managing your inbox, tracking priorities, summarizing meetings, preparing briefs, and filing expenses, you know it’s time that could be spent on customers and growth.


IrisGo learns these workflows by watching how you work, then automates them on your device. No repeated prompts, and your sensitive data stays on your device. Our Watch & Learn feature is central to understanding how you work, and handling that task forever. 

We’d love to learn:

  • Which of these tasks takes the most time in your day?

  • Was it clear on how to get started?

  • Where would you want more control or explanation?

Try the demo and let us know what works—or where you get stuck. We’ll be here to answer questions and learn from your feedback.


https://irisgo.ai/solopreneur

posts.name: Foley
posts.tagline: A voice to-do list that files, plans and asks first
posts.description: Say what needs doing. Foley turns it into a task with the project, date and reminder already set, and asks when it isn't sure instead of guessing. When plans change, say so and it moves the task. Ask it to plan your day, or what to work on first, and it answers from your list. Capture from your Apple Watch. The desktop app is free with no account, using your own OpenRouter key. Foley Pro runs the AI for you and syncs every device. On iPhone, Android, Mac, Windows and the web.

comments.body: Hi Product Hunt. I'm José, a software engineer with over 25 years of experience (https://www.linkedin.com/in/jose...). I kept losing tasks I said out loud: mid-meeting, in the car, walking the dog. Foley is the to-do list I wanted for that. You talk, and it files. It handles time the way people say it ("next Tuesday morning"), and it asks when it isn't sure instead of guessing. When plans change, say so and it moves the task. Ask it to plan your day, or what to work on first, and it answers from your own list. The desktop app is free with no account, using your own OpenRouter key. Foley Pro is $8 a month on the web, and your first month there is $4, applied at checkout. I'll be here all day. Tell me what it got wrong.
Using an Apple Watch to capture tasks is a nice touch. Sometimes pulling out your phone is already too much friction.
Finally an assistant can help organize the chaos in my head without making me type everything out.
can it handle task well even when plans change?

Handling relative time like "next Tuesday morning" is the part of voice capture that usually breaks first. Building voice AI for older adults, the trickiest case for us was self-corrections mid-sentence ("Thursday, no wait, Friday"). Does Foley treat the last thing said as the final intent, or does it ask you to confirm when it hears a correction like that?

"asks when it isn't sure instead of guessing" is the right default and most voice products get it backwards because asking feels like friction and guessing feels like magic, until the guess is wrong and now you've got a task filed under the wrong project with a made-up date. we fight the same tradeoff on calls at Dial. where's the line for you on what counts as "not sure", confidence score under some threshold, or ambiguity between two specific candidates like two projects with similar names?

posts.name: pmtui
posts.tagline: Autopilot for long-running AI sessions in terminal
posts.description: pmtui focuses on managing multiple agents and solving long-horizon tasks. Autopilot does what an agent loop does, except loops drift once the work runs long. So pmtui keeps the loop outside the agent and rebuilds the prompt each time from your goal and the agent's own last status. You choose how often to check back, and it only surfaces what really needs your attention

comments.body:
I manage 3-4 real projects these days, and paying constant attention to all of them is exhausting. Even with agents doing the work, I was still the one resolving every decision from Claude or Codex stopped on — including the trivial ones. That's the part I wanted to fix

pmtui runs an auto mode on top of the session. When a session stops on a decision, a 2nd claude/codex reads it, and if it's routine it answers — with the goal I set as context. You can think of it as using Claude to decide for another Claude when the decision doesn't need a human. The other half is keeping sessions alive without me. A daemon watches each tmux session and nudges it on a cadence I choose, building each prompt from that agent's own last status and my goal, instead of a generic "continue" that makes it re-plan or quit early.

posts.name: Cairo AI
posts.tagline: AI for human performance at work
posts.description: Cairo AI connects workforce analytics, skills intelligence, AI training, and simulations to help organizations develop their people. Each teammate takes a quick psychometric assessment and a weekly check-in, then gets their own trait cards, skill metrics, and AI-built development plans and practice scenarios. Spot friction, predict turnover, and test decisions like new hires before making them. Powered by Rosetta, our behavior model. Available on web, iOS, Android and Slack.

comments.body:
Hey Product Hunt! 👋 I'm Fernando Flores, founder of Cairo.

We started Cairo with a simple frustration: most companies know more about their software than about how their people actually work together. HR tools track headcount and run yearly surveys, but nobody can tell you why a great team clicks, why another one burns out, or what each person needs to grow.

So we built Cairo Teams, a Strava for human performance at work:

🧠 For every teammate: a quick psychometric assessment and a 2-minute weekly check-in unlock your own trait cards, skill metrics, and a development plan with AI-built courses and practice scenarios tailored to you.

📊 For leaders: team-level trends to spot friction early, anticipate turnover, and pressure-test decisions (like a new hire or a team reshuffle) before making them.

🔒 Privacy by design: individual check-in answers belong to the employee. Leaders only see trends, never personal responses. We think that's the only way people answer honestly.

Under the hood it runs on Rosetta, the behavior model we've been building to turn psychometric profiles into predictions about how people actually act.

Our approach evolved a lot along the way. We started closer to classic HR analytics and realized the product only works if employees want to open it, so we redesigned everything around the individual first and the dashboard second.

We've been lucky to get here with the support of the AWS Bridge Program, a research partnership with Universidad Panamericana to validate our metrics scientifically, and early customers like Swimotion who shaped the product.

It's live on web, iOS, Android and Slack.

posts.name: Hirevire
posts.tagline: Watch every applicant answer your questions
posts.description: Hirevire replaces first-round phone screens with async video, audio and text answers. Candidates need no login. New since our 2023 launch: 1. AI writes screening questions from your job title, or turns a pasted list into set-up questions. 2. AI drafts a scorecard from the job, then scores videos, answers and resumes. 3. Rerun a score with a note. General rules go to the job's scoring memory. 4. MCP server: create jobs, read scores and move candidates from Claude, ChatGPT or any MCP client.

comments.body:
Hi Product Hunt, I am Sanat, co-founder of Hirevire. We first launched here in July 2023. We are still a team of two in Mumbai: Nikhil builds the product and I do the rest.

Hirevire sends candidates a link. They record video, audio or text answers on their phone, with no login, and you review them when you have time.

The work since then has gone into making each step of setup and review take less time.

Setting up a job: type a job title and AI suggests screening questions, with a response type and duration for each one. You choose how many. If your questions are already in a Google Doc, paste the whole list and AI turns it into set-up questions, including multiple-choice options and required fields.

Setting up scoring: AI reads the job and its questions and drafts a scorecard with factors, weights and rubrics. You edit what you want. The AI then scores video and audio answers, text answers, and the candidate's resume.

Fixing a score: if you disagree with a score, rerun it and write why. If your note is a rule for the whole job, Hirevire saves it to that job's scoring memory and uses it for every future score. You can also rescore many candidates at once after you change the rubric.

Working from your AI assistant: our MCP server connects Claude, ChatGPT or any MCP client with one URL and OAuth.
